hypothesis: The CUDA chain's prompt attention (cc_attn_fk) stages each block of K and V into shared memory as f16 with one 4-byte load at a time, and at head dim 256 on a T4 the warps wait on those loads most of the time (one warp a scheduler). Starting 16 loads of 16 bytes before converting the first keeps the same bits and makes a long prompt faster.
command: bench.c built against c/ (make CUDA=1 CUDA_ARCH=sm_75, as bench build does); COLI_CUDA=1 COLI_GPUS=0 CUDA_EXPERT_GB=auto OMP_WAIT_POLICY=ACTIVE OMP_PROC_BIND=close ./qwen36-bench --model <model> --text promessi_sposi.txt --lengths 2048,3072,4096,5120,6144,7168,8192 --gen 128 --teacher

hardware.cpu: Intel(R) Xeon(R) CPU @ 2.00GHz (4 cores / 8 threads, 38.5 MiB L3) + NVIDIA Tesla T4 (15360 MiB, sm_75, up to PCIe Gen3 x16)
hardware.storage: Google Colab VM disk (the model downloaded to /content before the runs)
hardware.os: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (Google Colab, T4 high-RAM), CUDA 13.0 (nvcc V13.0.88), driver 580.82.07, gcc 13.3.0

config.scenario: the 8192-token prompt of the ladder up (2048, 3072, ... 8192 in one process, each followed by 128 teacher-forced words)
config.tok_s: prompt tokens / the prompt's seconds (bench's prefill_tps of the 8192 row)
config.engine_build: origin/dev c1c06ac6 + our 14 other open PRs (3cf06708, measure-only)

quality.method: make -C c check (macOS arm64); on the T4, make -C c cuda-chain-check (on origin/dev + this change and on the measured stack + this change) and make -C c cuda-test pass, and the chain's test fails when the 16-byte staging rounds toward zero (correctness.txt). Every run of both versions here has the same 8192-token fingerprint (13fc52094ee1426c); the nll of 1024 teacher-forced words after an 8192-token prompt is the same byte for byte (quality.txt)
